title: He screams in the fire.
paragraphs: Let that shatter the version of hell you’ve been fed by movies and myths. Because the Satan you see in culture—smiling, ruling, commanding demons—is not the one the Bible reveals.
And what it shows is terrifying.
“And the devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur… and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.” — Revelation 20:10

Not reigning.
Not laughing.
Not untouched.
Now here’s the question that grips the soul:
How can a spirit feel fire?
Because Satan is not human. He is not flesh and bone. So how does torment work?
Hell is not just about physical flames.
Jesus Himself described hell not as a metaphor, but as a place of real anguish:
“In Hades, being in torment… he lifted up his eyes…” — Luke 16:23

So when the Bible speaks of the “lake of fire,” it is not diminishing reality—it is intensifying it. Fire is the closest human language can get to describing what it means to be under the full, unfiltered justice of a holy God.

The deceiver.
The accuser.
The whisperer of your darkest temptations—
“Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.” — Matthew 25:41
Hell was not made for you.
But sin… drags humanity into the same judgment.
That’s the part we don’t like to hear.
Because we want a God who is loving—
Here’s where the fire meets grace.

Because every sin you’ve hidden…
every compromise you justified…
every secret no one else knows…
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
And the weight of that sin is not light.
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
Because the story doesn’t end there.
“…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
But that you don’t have to go there.
But because Jesus stepped into your place.
On the cross, He absorbed what we deserved.

The wrath.
The judgment.
The weight.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
So while Satan will face eternal torment—
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1
Let that sink into your bones.
So the real question isn’t just—
Because eternity is not a game.
“Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved…” — Acts 16:31
Not when you clean yourself up.
If this stirred something in your spirit—don’t ignore it.

Out of darkness.
Out of sin.
Out of the fire meant for the enemy—
If you’ve been playing with sin thinking it has no consequence—this is your wake-up call.
If you’ve been afraid of judgment—this is your doorway to freedom.
That’s exactly who grace is for.
Because one day, eternity won’t be a question.
